papers.title: Effect of Implant Surface and Radiation Dose on Crestal Bone Loss in Irradiated Patients: 1-Year Preliminary Outcomes.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Implant-supported prosthetic rehabilitation is frequently required in head and neck cancer patients but carries an elevated risk of impaired osseointegration and peri-implant bone loss. Hydrophilic implant surfaces have demonstrated improved early osseointegration in preclinical studies. However, clinical evidence, especially in irradiated patients, remains limited. This study aimed to compare short-term clinical and radiologic outcomes of hydrophilic implants versus conventional implants placed in irradiated bone. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, 107 implants (conventional surface: n=53; hydrophilic surface: n=54) were placed in 21 irradiated patients with head and neck cancer using a split-mouth design. Panoramic radiographs were obtained at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months, and mesial and distal crestal bone loss was assessed. Further, effects of implant surface and implant-specific radiation dose were evaluated. RESULTS: At 12 months, hydrophilic implants demonstrated significantly reduced crestal bone loss compared with conventional implants both mesially (0.6±0.7 versus 0.9±0.7 mm; P<0.001) and distally (0.5±0.4 versus 0.9±0.6 mm; P<0.001). Implant location and radiation-dose category did not show statistically significant associations with bone loss over time. CONCLUSIONS: Hydrophilic implant surfaces were associated with reduced early crestal bone loss in irradiated patients, while radiation dose exhibited no measurable impact within the first year. This study is the first to demonstrate a potential benefit of hydrophilic implants in irradiated patients, including those with autologous bone grafts. Hydrophilic implants may represent a promising option for implant rehabilitation in this high-risk patient population.

papers.title: Tunable mechanical properties of polymer-based surrogate materials for articular cartilage and vocal fold repair
papers.abstract: Abstract The macroscopic biomechanical characteristics of soft and ultrasoft tissues, such as articular cartilage and vocal folds, significantly determine their physiological function. Treatments of widespread tissue degradations due to osteoarthritis in the knee or vocal fold impairment remain an unresolved challenge. For the design of implants for tissue repair after injury or disease, the thorough understanding of the unique biomechanical properties of native tissues and potential substitute materials is essential. Based on large-strain mechanical testing methods combined with hyperelastic nonlinear continuum mechanics modeling and finite element simulations, we identify qualitative similarities between articular knee cartilage and vocal folds. Under compression, both tissue types show a strain-induced stiffening alongside hysteresis and conditioning. Based on synthetic metamaterials, we demonstrate that the replication of the complex mechanical properties, and thus the macroscopic mechanical functionality of the corresponding soft tissues, becomes possible. In accordance with native tissues, a pronounced nonlinear stress-strain behavior and stiffening is obtained, while hysteresis can be predominantly demonstrated for hybrid, polyolefin-hydrogel-based articular cartilage surrogates. We furthermore demonstrate the tunability of biomimetic stiffnesses of synthetic articular cartilage and vocal fold surrogates through tissue-specific process-material combinations. These involve complementary approaches based on adapting the density of load-bearing polyolefin networks in laser-sintered polypropylene-polyvinylpolypyrrolidone composites for cartilaginous properties, and the variation of the cross-linking density of synthetic silicone-based epithelium surrogates in ultrasoft vocal folds. These observations furthermore indicate the significance of viscous, hydrogel-based fractions for the biomimetic replication of hysteresis and relaxation. Our results therefore demonstrate the biomimetic similarity of soft tissues across a broad mechanical range alongside the feasibility of synthetic metamaterials in replicating essential passive biomechanical functions with great potential for future treatment options.

papers.title: AI-Driven Simulations of the Car Components Fatigue Life, for Automotive Predictive Maintenance Applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a new Integrated Framework for AI predictive Maintenance (AMIFAIM—Andrei Muresan Integrated Framework for AI predictive Maintenance), which allows online monitoring of the main components’ fatigue life. A Random Forest regressor, trained on 15,000 synthetic loading scenarios generated by physics-based superposition of seven finite element load cases, serves as a near-real-time surrogate for structural simulation. The framework is demonstrated on a lower control arm made from S420MC steel (EN 10149-2) in a Dacia Logan front suspension. The trained model predicts Von Mises stress from six strain-gauge channels with R2 = 0.9943, MAE = 28.76 MPa, and RMSE = 37.58 MPa on unseen test data, while providing uncertainty estimates per prediction from the variance in the ensemble. Leave-One-Load-Case-Out validation confirms generalisation to unseen load combinations (mean R2 = 0.950). Cumulative fatigue damage is tracked in real time using the Palmgren–Miner rule with an S-N curve calibrated for hot-spot stress conditions. Simulated drive scenarios confirm that the system correctly distinguishes between benign service (near-zero fatigue damage under highway loading) and abusive conditions (5–8% life consumption in 30 s under repeated impact loading), consistent with the expected behaviour of a properly designed suspension link. The entire pipeline—data augmentation, training, prediction, fatigue tracking, and visualisation—is driven by a single configuration file. Applying it to a new component requires only finite element results and material properties; no software changes are needed. The framework is designed to be reconfigured for components for which representative FEA load cases and material-fatigue inputs are available. The current implementation operates on FEA-derived virtual sensor data, with the architecture designed for direct replacement by physical strain-gauge hardware in future experimental validation.

papers.title: Rapid prediction of microscale stress fields in fiber-reinforced composites from limited finite element data using a deep learning framework
papers.abstract: Predicting transverse stress response of fiber-reinforced polymer composites at the microstructural level traditionally relies on finite element method (FEM) simulations of representative volume elements, which are computationally expensive and time-consuming. While deep learning offers a faster surrogate, most existing approaches require hundreds to thousands of FEM-generated training samples, creating a significant data bottleneck. The results demonstrate that accurate stress-contour prediction can be achieved using as few as 20 base representative volume element simulations, expanded to 80 training samples through rotation and reflection augmentation. To address this limited dataset and emphasize mechanically critical stress concentration regions, a two-stage U-Net framework with a dual-output head and a custom attention loss based on red–green–blue (RGB) pixel values was developed. The first stage trains the model on exaggerated stress contours to identify regions of peak stress, while the second refines predictions using standard stress contours to recover realistic stress magnitudes. Trained on 80 augmented samples derived from 20 base simulations, the model reproduced FEM-validated stress contours with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.366 ± 0.284 MPa and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.943 ± 0.006 . Expanding the base dataset to 85, yielding 340 augmented samples, reduced the MAE to 0.872 ± 0.168 MPa and increased the SSIM to 0.967 ± 0.004 . In both cases, inference took less than one second per sample, compared with 1620 s for a single FEM simulation.

papers.title: Effect of low-power remelting process on the formed specimen of TC4 titanium alloy by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the SLM remelting process and improved the overall performance of the formed samples greatly. It provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials such as TC4 on machines with limited laser power. By designing the experiment of the low-power remelting process (LPRP), the difference between direct high power forming quality and low power forming quality is explored. Which provides new considerations for SLM low-power forming TC4 specimens. Design/methodology/approach This experiment is based on energy density. In the experimental parameters, to ensure the sum of the remelting process energy density and the volume process forming energy density was consistent. Using different volume laser powers and remelting laser powers to form samples. Findings The authors found that using LPRP can form specimens with good surface quality and density, and the metallographic structure is beneficial to the mechanical properties. This method can use low-power equipment to form high melting point materials, reduce excessive energy gradients, produce multiple α' phases, and improve the overall performance of the specimen. Originality/value The LPRP has the following advantages: 1) Reduces the excessive energy gradient to produce multiple α' phases; 2) Provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials such as TC4 on machines with limited laser power.

papers.title: Challenging the Misch SA4 staging protocol: one-stage lateral sinus augmentation with simultaneous implants in sub-3-mm residual bone height – a split-mouth case report
papers.abstract: Objectives: This split-mouth case report evaluates the feasibility of simultaneous implant placement with lateral-window sinus augmentation in the severely atrophic posterior maxilla (Misch SA-4; residual bone height <3 mm), comparing two three-dimensional grafting strategies: an autogenous bone ring versus an allogeneic demineralized dentin block. Case presentation: A 52-year-old man presented with bilateral posterior maxillary atrophy (residual bone height: 2.8 mm on the right, 2.4 mm on the left). Simultaneous lateral sinus augmentation and implant placement were performed in a single surgical session. The left side received an autogenous corticocancellous bone ring harvested from the mandibular symphysis, while the contralateral side was reconstructed using a processed allogeneic demineralized dentin block. Tapered implants were placed into both graft types, achieving primary stability of 35 N·cm (autogenous) and 32 N·cm (allogeneic). Results: At the 6-month follow-up, both implants demonstrated osseointegration without peri-implant radiolucencies or sinus complications. Implant stability quotient values were 74 (autogenous) and 70 (allogeneic), both exceeding thresholds associated with predictable osseointegration. The patient remained asymptomatic throughout healing, and prosthetic rehabilitation was initiated. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that simultaneous implant placement with lateral window sinus augmentation can be successfully performed with residual bone heights below 3 mm when structural block grafts provide three-dimensional support. Both autogenous bone rings and allogeneic dentin blocks achieved comparable clinical outcomes, though the allogeneic option eliminates donor-site morbidity. While these findings support extending one-stage protocols to the extreme Misch SA4 spectrum, longer follow-up and larger comparative studies are needed to establish definitive recommendations.

papers.title: Toward a Population-Informed Framework for Structural Assessment of 3D-Printed Prosthetic Sockets
papers.abstract: Structural assessment of customized 3D-printed prosthetic sockets requires a basis for selecting geometries and loading relevant socket regions. This study explored a population-informed assessment framework combining statistical shape sampling with mock limb material comparisons. A statistical shape model (SSM) was reconstructed from 67 archived records of liner-covered residual limbs. Geometries at the empirical 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles of the first principal component guided socket design; mock limbs matched the socket inner surfaces. Nine finite element cases compared aluminum, a muscle-inspired surrogate, and a bulk soft-tissue surrogate under 4480 N loading based on ISO 10328 condition I at level P5. At the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th percentiles, trimline maxima were 1.0, 1.5, and 0.7 MPa for aluminum; 16.0, 12.4, and 3.9 MPa for the muscle-inspired surrogate; and 19.7, 14.1, and 3.9 MPa for the bulk surrogate. Whole-socket peaks shifted from the distal attachment with aluminum to the anterior trimline with compliant surrogates in two geometries; all materials produced distal peaks in the 97.5th-percentile geometry. These findings support combining patient-derived shape sampling with explicit mock limb specification for regional socket assessment. Shape percentiles describe observed variation rather than worst-case strength conditions. The framework may inform complementary test configurations, but failure prediction and product assurance require broader assessment and physical validation.

papers.title: Does cemented versus uncemented humeral stem fixation influence outcomes in primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty? An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background There is a diversity of opinion regarding the best method for humeral fixation in reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA). Traditionally, cemented stems have offered immediate fixation, while newer uncemented implants reduce the risks associated with bone cement. We undertook an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing cemented and uncemented humeral stems in primary RSA for patient-reported outcomes, range of movement, revision, complications, radiographic findings, and tuberosity healing. Methods A comprehensive database search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL and PubMed was conducted up to August 2025 and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Comparative (two-arm) studies formed the inferential basis; single-arm cohorts were pooled descriptively. The assessed outcomes included functional outcomes, radiological outcomes and range of motion. Random-effects models generated mean differences (MDs) and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed with the Risk of Bias in Non-Randomised Studies of Interventions tool (ROBINS-I) tool and certainty with GRADE. Leave-one-out sensitivity and funnel-plot analyses were performed where sufficient study-level data allowed. Results Forty-nine studies (21,420 shoulders; 11,204 cemented, 10,216 uncemented) were included, of which 22 were comparative. There were no significant between-group differences in abduction (MD 2.93°; 95% CI −1.06 to 6.92), forward flexion, external or internal rotation, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons, Constant–Murley or visual analogue pain scores, periprosthetic fracture, revision (OR 0.98; 95% CI 0.64 to 1.48) or tuberosity healing. papers.abstract: Large segmental craniofacial bone defects remain a major clinical challenge, and scaffold-based bone tissue engineering offers a promising regenerative strategy. This study comprehensively evaluated the biomechanical and hydrodynamic properties of gradient-porosity triply periodic minimal surface polyether ether ketone scaffolds across 5 geometries (Diamond, Gyroid, Schwarz, Split P, and Lidinoid) for bone defect repair. The scaffolds were designed as cylindrical gradient-porosity constructs (10 mm in diameter and 10 mm in height). A low porosity (50%) was maintained within the 2-mm peripheral zone to provide mechanical support, whereas the central region (3-mm radius) featured higher porosities (50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%) to enhance mass transport. Mechanical behavior was evaluated by uniaxial compression testing and finite element analysis under compressive and rotational loads, and hydrodynamic behavior was assessed by computational fluid dynamics. The Lidinoid and Diamond scaffolds exhibited the highest construct stiffness. Increasing the central porosity reduced both compressive and rotational stiffness and amplified stress concentrations at the porosity transition zones. The highest peak von Mises stresses were observed in the Schwarz scaffolds under compressive loading and in the Diamond scaffolds under rotational loading. Higher central porosity increased permeability and reduced the inlet-to-outlet pressure differential. The Schwarz and Split P scaffolds showed the highest permeability, whereas the Gyroid and Split P scaffolds maintained the most uniform velocity distributions. In conclusion, both the geometry and the gradient-porosity significantly influenced scaffold behavior. The Split P scaffolds offered the best balance between biomechanical and hydrodynamic performance, highlighting their potential for clinical translation in craniofacial bone defect repair.

papers.abstract: Engineering functional skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle tissues requires the integration of advanced biofabrication technologies with physiologically relevant maturation strategies. This review provides an integrated overview of biofabrication and bioreactor-based maturation strategies for muscle tissue engineering. We discuss how muscle-specific requirements influence biomaterial selection, construct architecture, and stimulation approaches, and summarize recent advances in biofabrication and mechanical, electrical, perfusion, and multimodal bioreactor systems. papers.abstract: Abstract: Background: Direct anterior approach total hip arthroplasty (DAA-THA) is associated with postoperative heterotopic ossification (HO), which may impair joint function. Inflammation and oxidative stress are important contributors to HO development. Danxiong Huoxue Tablets (DHT) possess potential anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, but their effects on postoperative HO remain insufficiently investigated. Objectives: This preclinical study aimed to evaluate the effects of DHT on experimental HO and to explore its possible association with inflammatory and oxidative stress-related signaling using a rat DAA-induced HO model and an osteogenic differentiation model of human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs). Methods: A rat DAA-induced HO model was established and treated with low- and high-dose DHT for 28 days. X-ray and histological analyses were used to evaluate ectopic bone formation. ELISA and Western blotting were employed to assess inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β), oxidative stress biomarkers (SOD, GSH-Px, MDA) and related signaling proteins (NF-κB p65, NLRP3, Nrf2, HO-1). In parallel, hBMSCs were used to examine the effects of DHT on cell viability, osteogenic differentiation and related molecular changes. Results: DHT administration reduced ectopic bone formation in the rat HO model, as confirmed by imaging and histological analyses. DHT also decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, improved oxidative stress-related markers, reduced NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway-related protein expression and increased Nrf2/HO-1 expression. In-vitro, DHT suppressed hBMSC osteogenic differentiation and downregulated Runx2, Osterix, BMP-2 and OCN expression. Conclusion: DHT attenuated experimental DAA-induced HO in rats and inhibited osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs, possibly by reducing inflammatory responses and oxidative stress. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of DHT as a potential adjunctive strategy for preventing postoperative HO.

papers.title: Estimation of a countably infinite-dimensional transition probability matrix using a stick-breaking prior
papers.abstract: Abstract We consider the problem of estimation of the transition probability matrix (TPM) of a Markov chain where the state space is countably infinite. At present, there is no methodology in the literature for direct estimation of infinite-dimensional TPMs. Standard approaches, including maximum likelihood estimation and Bayesian methods based on Dirichlet priors, are inherently finite-state and, when applied in this setting, assign zero probability to all unobserved transitions. To derive a method for estimation of infinite-dimensional TPMs, we propose a Bayesian nonparametric approach that employs a random measure prior. Specifically, we utilize hierarchical and generalized hierarchical stick-breaking processes as priors on the rows of the TPM. The generalized hierarchical stick-breaking prior, in particular, allow for both positive and negative correlations among any pair of transition probabilities, thereby enabling more realistic modeling of the dependence across the state transitions. We develop a blocked Gibbs sampling algorithm for posterior computation under a generalized hierarchical stick-breaking prior that is fast, highly efficient, and well suited to large-scale problems. The proposed method is evaluated through extensive simulations as well as applications to real-world datasets on historical trading volume for the United States Oil Fund (USO), and daily precipitation records from Heathrow, London. The empirical results demonstrate strong and stable predictive performance in all scenarios considered.

papers.title: Bayesian neural network with autoencoder for model-based description of α -particle preformation factor
papers.abstract: $α$ decay is an important probe for studying the structure of heavy and superheavy nuclei, in which the $α$-particle preformation ($P_α$) is a key physical quantity for describing decay half-lives. This work develops a hybrid framework that integrates Bayesian neural networks with autoencoder (BNN-Auto), combined with the cosh potential (CPT), to systematically optimize the constraint and prediction of $P_α$. The model employs variational inference for probabilistic modeling of network weights, naturally providing robust uncertainty quantification for predictions, and utilizes an autoencoder to enhance the robustness of feature representation. Based on experimental data from 535 nuclei, the BNN-Auto method achieves relative improvements in the root mean square deviation ($σ_{\rm{RMS}}$) of $P_α$ prediction by $61.14\%$ on the training set and $54.49\%$ on the validation set. Further analysis reveals that the $P_α$ and half-life extracted by the model exhibit pronounced odd-even staggering and shell effects in isotopic chains with $Z=86-90$ and isotones with $N=124-128$ and $N=150-154$. Moreover, we successfully predict the $α$ decay half-lives of nuclei with $Z=120$ and observe a significant increase in the half-life near $N=184$, which verifies the shell effect of the predicted 'stable island'. This study not only provides a high-precision theoretical description for $α$ decay, but also offers a new machine learning perspective for exploring the structure of superheavy nuclei.

papers.title: Variational Graph Neural Networks for Uncertainty Quantification in Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasingly wide use of deep machine learning techniques in computational mechanics has significantly accelerated simulations of problems that were considered unapproachable just a few years ago. However, in critical applications such as Digital Twins for engineering or medicine, fast responses are not enough; reliable results must also be provided. In certain cases, traditional deterministic methods may not be optimal as they do not provide a measure of confidence in their predictions or results, especially in inverse problems where the solution may not be unique or the initial data may not be entirely reliable due to the presence of noise, for instance. Classic deep neural networks also lack a clear measure to quantify the uncertainty of their predictions. In this work, we present a variational graph neural network (VGNN) architecture that integrates variational layers into its architecture to model the probability distribution of weights. Unlike computationally expensive full Bayesian networks, our approach strategically introduces variational layers exclusively in the decoder, allowing us to estimate cognitive uncertainty and statistical uncertainty at a relatively lower cost. In this work, we validate the proposed methodology in two cases of solid mechanics: the identification of the value of the elastic modulus with nonlinear distribution in a 2D elastic problem and the location and quantification of the loads applied to a 3D hyperelastic beam, in both cases using only the displacement field of each test as input data. The results show that the model not only recovers the physical parameters with high precision, but also provides confidence intervals consistent with the physics of the problem, as well as being able to locate the position of the applied load and estimate its value, giving a confidence interval for that experiment.

papers.title: A human‐in‐the‐loop Bayesian optimization framework for constraint‐aware bioprocess development
papers.abstract: Abstract We present Pareto Front Guided Sampling (PFGS), a human‐in‐the‐loop (HiL) Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework that reformulates surrogate‐model predictions as a multi‐objective optimization problem, allowing domain knowledge to be added intuitively to any BO problem. PFGS addresses constrained optimization by treating the posterior probability of constraint satisfaction as an explicit Pareto objective, and robust optimization via a Monte Carlo estimate of expected lower‐confidence performance under input perturbations, capturing likely degradation. The multi‐dimensional Pareto front makes trade‐offs between predicted performance, model uncertainty, constraint satisfaction, and robustness visible through pairwise two‐dimensional projections on an interactive dashboard, allowing selection criteria to be refined as the model and objectives evolve. The framework is showcased on a eight‐dimensional in‐silico fed‐batch Chinese Hamster Ovary cell culture case study. We showed improved performance over BO when the expert has perfect domain knowledge; however, PFGS is not designed to outperform BO, but rather to present a HiL acquisition function framework.

papers.title: Digital twin-driven multi-objective optimization of milling parameters under small-sample conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the high experimental cost, insufficient parameter-space coverage, and multi-objective trade-off difficulties in milling parameter optimization under small-sample conditions, this study proposes a digital twin-driven multi-objective optimization method for milling parameters. An end-milling process is considered, with spindle speed, feed rate, axial depth of cut, and radial depth of cut selected as input parameters. A unified virtual evaluation interface is constructed to rapidly evaluate machining time, cutting force, and the probability of satisfying surface quality constraints. To improve parameter-space coverage, a diffusion-inspired noise-perturbation augmentation method is used to generate supplementary samples, which are further filtered using parameter bounds and cutting-force physical consistency constraints. A Gaussian process regression model is then established as a surface roughness threshold classification model, transforming surface quality evaluation into a probabilistic constraint satisfaction problem. Based on the virtual evaluation model, Bayesian optimization and a multi-objective genetic algorithm are combined to search for Pareto non-dominated solutions. The case study shows that the proposed method can generate a relatively continuous set of trade-off solutions among machining time, cutting force, and surface quality feasibility, providing alternative parameter combinations for different machining preferences. The optimization results are further integrated into a digital twin visualization system for interactive comparison and decision support. The recommended parameter combinations still require further validation through physical machining experiments.

papers.abstract: The purposes of this research article were 1) to develop a competency-based learning assessment model; 2) to evaluate the competency-based learning assessment model; and 3) to improve the competency-based learning assessment model in mathematics for Prathom Suksa 6 students in schools under the Kalasin Primary Educational Service Area Office. The research employed a research and development methodology, divided into several steps: in the process of developing the evaluation model, the target group consisted of 5 experts, 3 teachers, and 43 students, selected using purposive sampling; for implementation and evaluation step of the evaluation model, the target group consisted of 9 teachers and 186 students, selected through purposive sampling and the refinement of the evaluation model. The primary informants were the 9 teachers, selected through purposive sampling from the implementation and evaluation phase of the evaluation model. The research results found that 1) the competency-based learning assessment model consisted of 7 components: (1) assessment objectives, (2) content to be assessed, (3) assessment indicators and criteria, (4) assessment methods, (5) assessment tools, (6) assessors, and (7) reporting results and providing feedback; 2) the results of the assessment of the model's effectiveness found that overall it was at a high level ( = 4.45, S.D.=0.62), and the results of the study of teachers' satisfaction with the model found that overall it was at a high level ( = 4.13, S.D. = 0.88); and 3) the results of improving the assessment model summarized the points for improvement as follows: (1) assessment tools for students to assess themselves and peers to assess students, using different versions of the tools; (2) the assessment scores were weighted differently, categorized according to the assessors, with teachers having higher weight than students' self-assessments and peer assessments; and (3) the learning management guidelines to develop students' competencies used any active learning method that can integrate competencies (KSA) appropriately in the local context that was connected to real life, and emphasized creating situations for students to actually do things so that students can develop their competencies to their full potential. The results of this study will be useful to the Primary Educational Service Area Offices in Kalasin Province to use this model to determine policies, plans, projects, and activities in preparing for the use of the curriculum, learning management, and competency-based learning assessment in the future.

papers.title: An Object-Level Active Semantic-Driven Posterior Probability Change Detection Method for Remote Sensing Images with Limited Annotations
papers.abstract: Change detection in high-resolution remote sensing imagery is susceptible to the adverse effects of within-class spectral heterogeneity, shadows, and complex spatial structures. Meanwhile, change detection methods based on land-cover posterior probabilities generally rely on reliable semantic training information, making complete manual interpretation costly. To address these issues, this study develops a change detection framework that integrates SEEDS-guided SAM object construction and active learning-based interpretation with FCM-CSBN-CVAPS posterior probability inference. First, representative points of SEEDS superpixels are used as prompts for SAM to generate candidate objects and construct a mutually exclusive object partition. Second, based on the spectral statistical features of the superpixels and an XGBoost classifier, active learning is employed to select highly uncertain samples for limited manual annotation, thereby obtaining object-level semantic information. Finally, FCM is used to characterize pixel-level spectral uncertainty, while CSBN incorporates spatial context to estimate posterior probabilities of land-cover classes. Bi-temporal change measurement and changed-area extraction are then performed in the posterior probability space. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves stable change detection performance by manually annotating only approximately 10% of the superpixels in the target scenes. On DS1, DS2, and DS3, the Kappa coefficients reach 83.87%, 86.05%, and 90.21%, respectively, while the corresponding F1 scores are 87.62%, 91.78%, and 91.31%, achieving the highest Kappa and F1 scores among the evaluated methods under the specified experimental settings. These results indicate an effective balance between false-alarm suppression and missed-detection control for change detection using limited target-scene semantic annotations. In adaptive evaluation experiments, the mean Kappa and F1 scores reach 84.58% and 87.84%, respectively, further confirming the effectiveness and stability of the proposed framework across diverse remote sensing scenarios.

papers.abstract: This paper examines the implementation of fake papers analysis as a pedagogical strategy for academic literacy development across five consecutive cohorts of undergraduate students of political sciences and international relations at the Universidad del CEMA, Argentina (2022–2026, n=60), using qualitative analysis of student written productions and self-assessment records in a longitudinal design. Findings indicate that students across all cohorts consistently identified formal and structural errors, but only those equipped with explicit methodological scaffolding demonstrated precision in detecting deeper methodological inconsistencies. These results extend the literature on evaluative judgement and active learning by identifying methodological scaffolding, rather than exposure to flawed texts alone, as the key mediating condition for critical literacy development. The study offers practitioners a replicable, low-resource instructional sequence in which scaffolding tools precede fake papers analysis, resulting in measurable gains in students’ capacity to identify methodological inconsistencies and produce more coherent academic writing.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for meteorological services in the low-altitude economy: Progress, challenges, and future directions
papers.abstract: The rapid development of the low-altitude economy demands better meteorological services to support unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), electric vertical take-off and landings aircraft (eVTOLs), and urban air mobility systems (UAM). The current meteorological services are not sufficient to predict highly variable atmospheric conditions at low altitudes, where accurate meteorological data is critical for safe and efficient low-altitude economic activities. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance low-altitude meteorology by improving atmospheric observation, high-resolution weather prediction, risk assessment, and flight-oriented decision support. However, existing studies have largely focused on individual AI applications, and their contributions to meteorological services for low-altitude operations have not been comprehensively reviewed. This review summarizes recent advances in AI applications to connect low-altitude meteorology, atmospheric observation, weather prediction, and weather risk assessment with low-altitude flight operations. We discuss AI applications in multi-source atmospheric sensing, microscale environmental reconstruction, high-resolution prediction, weather risk quantification, and weather-aware flight operations, and further highlight emerging directions including physics-informed AI, foundation models, digital twins, and autonomous AI agents. Beyond improving meteorological prediction, we emphasize that AI should facilitate the transformation of atmospheric information into flight-relevant knowledge by linking environmental conditions with aircraft responses. Finally, we identify major challenges related to data availability, model generalization, uncertainty quantification, and practical deployment. This review provides a novel perspective on the integration of atmospheric science and AI for developing future meteorological services that support safer and more efficient low-altitude transportation.

papers.title: The Application of AI/ML and IIoT to Predictive Maintenance
papers.abstract: Predictive maintenance has emerged as a critical approach to industrial automation, particularly as a part of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) where real-time monitoring and smart analytics are key to reducing downtime and maximizing operational performance. The fault-tolerant predictive maintenance framework of air compressors based on probabilistic Hidden Markov Model (HMM) combined with IIoT-based sensor data is introduced in this paper. In the suggested model, these parameters are critical variables that are monitored to identify any onset of degradation and thus predict possible failures: vibration, temperature, pressure, acoustic signals and motor current. The system identifies the compressor conditions in six operational states (S0–S5), which makes it possible to dynamically make decisions and plan maintenance activities. The comparative performance examination demonstrates that the suggested HMM model has higher accuracy (96.3%), precision (95.6%), and recall (94.9%) in contrast to conventional approaches, Random Forest (93.1%), and LSTM (95.2%) models. It also gives a better lead time to failure identification (7.8 hours), 22.4 percent downtime reduction, and 18.7 percent maintenance cost savings. The uncertainty quantification and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation are also considered in the model, which can ensure its robustness in face of sensor anomalies. The study proves that the application of machine learning, together with the IIoT infrastructure, enables a significant enhancement of predictive maintenance of industrial air compressor systems in order to ensure a higher level of reliability, a reduction of operationalcosts, and more intelligent asset management.

papers.title: Mechanical Properties and Collaborative Design of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Structures with Variable Density and Variable Direction
papers.abstract: This paper separately investigates the effects of variable density and variable direction design on the quasistatic compressive response of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures and subsequently proposes an integrated optimization strategy. First, the variable density design is investigated. The elastic modulus remains nearly constant at 295 MPa across all gradients, but increasing the linear gradient coefficient from 0.5 to 1.5 reduces the yield strength and plateau stress by 13.4% and 11.3%, respectively, while total energy absorption varies by merely ±1.34%. Then, the variable direction design is analyzed. Rotating the lattice to 45° increases the elastic modulus by 39.6% to 416 MPa and raises the specific energy absorption by 43.6% to 64.2 J/g, which confirms that load capacity and load uniformity can be independently adjusted. Based on these findings, a series of TPMS structures combining variable density and variable direction is constructed. In the three‐point bending test, the peak load of the 2D optimized beam increased by 27.79% compared with the uniform beam. However, for the supporting beam, the peak load and energy absorption of the 3D optimized beam improved by 15.36% and 19.83%, respectively.

papers.title: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block with lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) block versus fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) for hip surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Effective analgesia that preserves motor function is essential for early mobilization after hip surgery. Although fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is recommended for total hip arthroplasty, the comparative efficacy of combined pericapsular nerve group and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve blocks (PENG + LFCN) remains uncertain. Methods: Databases including Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Central, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched up to December 8, 2024. Statistical analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) (computer program, version 5.4, The Cochrane Collaboration, 2020). Results: Seven randomized controlled trials involving 572 participants were included. Compared with FICB, PENG + LFCN significantly reduced static pain at 12 hours (mean difference [MD] = −0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], −0.28 to −0.11; P < .0001) and dynamic pain at 6 hours (MD = −0.87; 95% CI, −1.64 to −0.10; P = .03) and 48 hours (MD = −0.26; 95% CI, −0.49 to −0.02; P = .03). It also lowered quadriceps weakness (odds ratio = 0.09; 95% CI, 0.04–0.21; P < .00001), improved limb strength (MD = 1.03; 95% CI, 0.05–2.01; P = .04), reduced patient-controlled intravenous analgesia frequency (MD = −1.64; 95% CI, −3.13 to −0.15; P = .03), and shortened mobilization time (MD = −9.04; 95% CI, −14.28 to −3.80; P = .0007). Conclusion: PENG + LFCN may provide superior early analgesia and better preserve lower-limb motor function than FICB after hip surgery. However, the evidence is limited by few trials, small sample sizes, and substantial heterogeneity. Larger, adequately powered trials are warranted.

papers.title: Honeycombs Across Material Classes: A Mechanism‐Based Review of Design Strategies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Honeycomb cores and related lattice and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide lightweight load support, energy absorption, recovery, and multifunctionality, but their performance can degrade when material, manufacturing route, interfaces, or component boundaries change. This review examines how cell‐wall bending, buckling, folding, self‐contact, and load transfer interact across service conditions. Studies of conventional, auxetic, chiral, graded, hierarchical, and folded honeycombs, sandwich panels, and related lattice and TPMS structures made from polymers, polymer composites, metals, and ceramics are compared at three levels: cell‐scale mechanisms, progressive‐collapse control, and structural integration. Geometry biases the available deformation modes, while constitutive behavior, rate sensitivity, fracture, viscoelasticity, reinforcement, interfaces, and manufacturing defects influence the active mode and collapse sequence. Curvature, grading, hierarchy, folding, multimaterial design, and reinforcement can redistribute deformation and delay localization, subject to initial peak force, densification strain, joint integrity, and process variability. Transfer from cells to components requires characterization of as‐manufactured geometry, defects, face‐core load transfer, environmental exposure, repeated loading, and service‐level validation. The review therefore separates geometry‐driven improvements from manufacturing effects and specifies a qualification path from material coupons and cells to panels and components.

papers.title: Microstructure and Corrosion Behavior of Laser-Remelted Ti-35Nb(-Sn) Alloys
papers.abstract: Abstract Ti-35Nb-Sn alloys are being investigated for biomedical applications as hard tissue replacements due to their reduced elastic modulus, which is closer to that of natural bone, and helping to minimize stress shielding and bone resorption. Laser remelting is a promising processing route for the manufacture of implants with a graded elastic modulus and optimized performance. This study investigates the impact of laser processing on the microstructure and corrosion resistance of Ti-35Nb alloys containing 0, 2, and 4 wt.% Sn. Microstructural morphology, chemical composition, and phase formation were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and x-ray diffraction (XRD), respectively. Corrosion resistance of the alloys was assessed in the base metal, heat-affected zone (HAZ), and fusion zone (FZ) using linear polarization tests in a physiological saline solution, using a three-electrode setup and an in-house developed microcell with a mask to limit the exposed area. Laser processing increased the fraction of the β phase in the alloys through reversion of strain-induced α ″ martensite and through elemental partitioning in the fusion zone, where Nb enrichment stabilized the β phase in dendrite cores. Under the tested conditions, laser processing did not seem to degrade the corrosion performance of Ti-35Nb and Ti-35Nb-2Sn, maintaining or shifting E corr and E pit to more noble values with similar or slightly reduced corrosion current densities. In contrast, the addition of 4 wt.% Sn had a detrimental effect, shifting E corr and E pit to more negative values, reducing polarization resistance, and increasing corrosion current densities by up to 10 × . In this alloy, laser processing promoted elemental segregation in the fusion zone, favoring localized corrosion in Sn-rich interdendritic regions. This work provides a deeper understanding of the relationships between laser processing, microstructure, and corrosion performance in laser-treated niobium-stabilized β-titanium alloys.

papers.title: Hierarchical Coordinated Path-Following Control of Four-Wheel Steer-by-Wire Vehicles with Corner Module Actuation
papers.abstract: Four-wheel steer-by-wire vehicles enable independent steering actuation at each corner, providing greater control flexibility for coordinated vehicle motion and path following. However, finite actuator dynamics and local steering loads can affect the wheel angles actually delivered to the vehicle, thereby influencing the overall steering response. To address this issue, this paper proposes a three-layer hierarchical steering control strategy for coordinated vehicle motion and accurate corner-level execution in four-wheel steer-by-wire vehicles. First, model predictive control (MPC) generates coordinated front- and rear-axle steering commands using weights calibrated offline by particle swarm optimization (PSO) and bounded state-dependent corrections from a fuzzy neural network (FNN) to the preview curvature and yaw rate references. Second, instantaneous-center-of-rotation (ICR) geometry converts the axle commands into four-wheel reference angles, accounting for differences between the turning radii of the left and right wheels and maintaining geometric consistency. Finally, active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) improves the execution performance of four independent permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) steering modules driven by field-oriented control (FOC), enabling wheel reference tracking and compensation for local steering-load disturbances. Simulations under representative driving conditions show that the mean lateral root-mean-square (RMS) error under ideal steering execution is 0.0278 m, 55.4% lower than that of the two-wheel-steering baseline. Regarding the finite corner actuator dynamics and the associated execution controllers, the worst-case lateral RMS error is 0.0631 m, still 27.9% lower than the same baseline, while the peak vehicle sideslip angle remains below 2.30°, with the applicability of the proposed framework at higher speeds and the capability limitations of the steering execution system also analyzed and discussed. These results show that the proposed hierarchical control framework improves the lateral path-following performance of four-wheel steer-by-wire vehicles with corner module actuation and enhances steering control flexibility across different driving scenarios.

papers.title: Circular Transitions in Industrial Design: From Electronic Disassembly to Biofabrication of Materials
papers.abstract: The transition to a circular economy requires a radical rethinking of industrial design methodologies, shifting the focus from anthropocentrism to a Planet-Oriented approach. This essay analyzes two fundamental and complementary trajectories of sustainability in contemporary design, exploring the management of technical and biological cycles. The first line investigates Design for Disassembly (DfD) applied to complex electronic devices, a critical sector characterized by alarming rates of e-waste and a dispersive management of Critical Raw Materials (CRMs). Through the analysis of the EN 45554 standard, the eDiM metric and the frontiers of active disassembly using shape memory materials, a framework is outlined to optimize the recovery of components with high technological value. The second trajectory explores the sphere of biological cycles, analyzing mycelium-based composites (MBC) and agricultural waste for furniture design. The thermodynamics of bio-fabrication are examined, demonstrating how advanced hot pressing techniques allow to achieve mechanical performance comparable to traditional engineered panels, with a lower net environmental impact assessed through Life Cycle Assessment logics. Through the Material Driven Design approach, the exhibition highlights the peculiar aesthetic, acoustic and phenomenological values of these biomaterials. Finally, the role of the Digital Product Passport (DPP) as an essential digital infrastructure to track and enable the circularity of both supply chains is analyzed, operating as a bridge between the regulatory compliance of the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation and design practice.

papers.title: Addressing Data Scarcity and Class Imbalance Using Active Learning and Synthetic Data Generation: Experimentation on Clinical Datasets
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of Machine Learning (ML) technologies has revolutionized healthcare, particularly in the domains of disease prediction and diagnosis. Nevertheless, some data-related issues, such as annotated data scarcity, low-quality labels, and class imbalance in the dataset, can compromise the effectiveness of the learning process. This paper first gives an overview of Active Learning (AL), which is a strategy in machine learning that helps models to achieve better performance using fewer labeled examples. It then reviews various strategies for addressing dataset imbalance, in particular focusing on data-level rebalancing approaches. The paper provides a review of existing works on active learning in the presence of class imbalance and on the integration of active learning with synthetic oversampling techniques. The central core of the paper is the implementation of four different strategies for data selection from publicly available clinical datasets: Random, Random + SMOTE, Uncertainty, and Uncertainty + SMOTE. We calculated and plotted balanced accuracy and average precision by iterating over 20 different seed values, using cumulative batches of labeled data, for each combination of dataset and classifier. Moreover we also carried out a statistical test to assess the extent to which the difference between the Random and Uncertainty distributions, and that between the Uncertainty and Uncertainty + SMOTE distributions, was statistically significant. Experiments show that uncertainty-based strategy can improve predictive performance compared with random acquisition, particularly with Random Forest, although the observed benefits vary across datasets, classifiers, performance metrics, and annotation budgets. The additional contribution of SMOTE is also context dependent and does not yield statistically significant improvements over uncertainty-based acquisition alone. For the WBCD dataset, it can be seen that Uncertainty + SMOTE is comparable to, or in some cases below, the uncertainty-only strategy. Metrics such as precision, recall, specificity, F1-score, AUROC and AUPRC are evaluated and provided.

papers.title: Coaxial Monitoring of Meltpool for Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Control
papers.abstract: Reliable process monitoring is critical for advancing laser powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M), as it provides the process information required for corrective control actions to prevent defects such as lack-of-fusion and keyhole porosity. A promising approach for PBF-LB/M process monitoring is coaxial measurement of light emitted from the meltpool area. More than two hundred research studies on coaxial monitoring of the meltpool have been performed, but there is still no validated and reliable method for measuring a suitable variable that could be directly used as an input for high-resolution control of the PBF-LB/M process, enabling process parameters such as laser power and scan speed to be dynamically adjusted not only at the part level, but locally for individual micrometer-scale segments along the scan track. This work reviews existing research studies on coaxial meltpool monitoring and identifies potential future research and development directions toward a standard and reliable meltpool monitoring method. Meltpool depth is identified as a particularly promising control-relevant variable. With the ability to monitor and control meltpool depth, it is possible to avoid undesirable process conditions due to too high or too low energy input, which would result in defects like keyhole porosity or lack-of-fusion. However, only five studies have attempted to estimate the melt pool depth coaxially during the PBF-LB/M process. Despite these attempts, there is no sufficiently validated method for high-resolution coaxial monitoring of meltpool depth in PBF-LB/M. The potential solution seems to be in combining concepts and recent discoveries from two-color coaxial camera- and photodiode-based meltpool area monitoring approaches. Based on the existing literature and hands-on experiences with establishing and working with coaxial monitoring systems, this work also provides guidelines and lists the most common challenges for implementing coaxial monitoring of the meltpool in the PBF-LB/M process.

papers.abstract: Precise nutrient management in avocado orchards requires accurate and interpretable predictions of leaf nitrogen content. In this study, explainable machine-learning models integrating spectral reflectance (350–2500 nm) and multispectral spatial features were comparatively evaluated for non-destructive estimation of avocado leaf nitrogen content. Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR) and one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) models were first developed using only spectral reflectance data as a baseline. To incorporate spatial–spectral information, multispectral images were arranged into cubes and processed with a 3D-CNN to extract deep features. These features were subsequently fused with the original spectral data to form a combined dataset. Both PLSR and 1D-CNN models were retrained using the fused inputs. The CNN hyperparameters were fine-tuned using Bayesian optimization, achieving a prediction R2 of 0.73 and an RMSE of 0.92 mg/g, which was comparable to the conventional PLSR model. The fusion approach showed numerically better performance than models based solely on spectra, suggesting spatial context may provide complementary information relevant to nitrogen estimation. Explainable artificial intelligence techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations and Integrated Gradients, identified 745 nm (red-edge), 994 nm (near-infrared), and 2459 nm (shortwave infrared), together with deep spatial features extracted from multispectral image cubes, as the most important predictors of nitrogen content in avocado leaves.

papers.abstract: In the context of high uncertainty and turbulence of the Russian stock market, scientifically based approaches to assessing the investment attractiveness of public companies are of particular importance, taking into account both fundamental operational indicators and a wide range of external macroeconomic, competitive, regulatory and geopolitical factors. This study is devoted to the development of an innovative methodology that integrates traditional methods of multiplicative and discounted analysis with modern machine learning algorithms and stochastic modeling, which allows us to move from point estimates to probabilistic intervals of fair value, adaptive to changing market regimes. The paper systematizes 50 key cost drivers, divided into endogenous (operational and financial metrics, logistics infrastructure, monetization) and exogenous (macroeconomic indicators, competitive environment, regulatory changes, force majeure), and using methods of gradient boosting, LASSO regression and Bayesian optimization, their weight ranges are determined, which allowed to build a multi-level hierarchy of influence on the market capitalization. The proposed system of eight interrelated mathematical formulas includes stochastic dynamics of key indicators (turnover, operating profit, customer base), nonlinear interactions between growth drivers, multiplicative adjustments to geopolitical and competitive risks (taking into account the GPR and EPU indices), corporate governance awards, ESG rating, technological sovereignty and intellectual property, and There is also discounting of projected free cash flows over the medium-term horizon. Dynamic calibration of the weights is carried out through a multifactorial regime classifier that takes into account market volatility, inflation differential, business activity and technical indicators, which ensures that the model adapts to different phases of the economic cycle. Practical verification based on historical data (2010-2026) showed high predictive accuracy (R2=0.93, RMSE≈135 rubles, MAPE=3.8%), and the final confidence interval of the fair value of shares obtained using the Bayesian approach demonstrated the practical applicability of the developed tool for substantiating investment decisions, risk management and scenario planning in conditions of high uncertainty.

papers.title: Degradation- and Inventory-Aware Hierarchical Frequency Control of PEM Fuel Cells and Electrolyzers in Low-Inertia Microgrids
papers.abstract: PEM fuel cells and electrolyzers can support frequency in low-inertia microgrids, but a switched-off unit needs time to start, every start–stop cycle degrades the stack, and a hydrogen chain with about 30% round-trip efficiency drains its tank even at zero net energy exchange. This paper proposes a degradation- and inventory-aware hierarchical frequency controller: a rate-aware tube model predictive control (MPC) power layer; a commitment layer that applies the classical ski-rental rule with break-even times derived from stack degradation and standby costs (commitment cost bounded by twice the offline optimum plus one start, excluding frequency performance); and a hydrogen-inventory layer that shifts the conventional-unit schedule to hold the tank level. On an electrochemical plant with a realistic information structure and 48 unseen test cases, the controller matches the frequency performance of a perfect-foresight commitment at 5% higher cost and reduces the integral absolute frequency error by 26% versus fuel-cell-only standby, 19% versus a tuned hold-time rule and 28–36% versus tuned PI, PID, fractional-order PID, fuzzy and MPC controllers. The gain grows with the electrolyzer start-up time and persists under random plant–model mismatch. Against a hold-time rule tuned on hour-long profiles, however, the frequency advantage is minimal; the remaining benefits are lower cost and the absence of cold electrolyzer onsets. Over ten days, the inventory layer keeps the tank within 1.09–1.29 kg; without it, the tank empties after 17–20 h.

papers.title: Adaptive Model Predictive Control with Delay Compensation and Online DAB Gain Estimation for a Synergetic Isolated VIENNA Rectifier
papers.abstract: The synergetic isolated VIENNA rectifier (SynC-VR-i) shapes its grid currents through two dual active bridges (DABs) fed from a split DC link of 10 µF per capacitor. Errors in the DAB power model therefore quickly appear as grid-current distortion. This paper proposes a delay-compensated adaptive model predictive control (MPC) scheme. A unit-invariant normalized-gradient estimator identifies the power gain of each DAB online, and the adapted model is used for both prediction and delay compensation. Under a positive-power excitation condition, the gain estimates are proven to converge exponentially to a neighborhood set by the power-model error. Local stability of the periodic switched operating point is estimated numerically along simulated orbits with the monodromy matrix, because frozen-time eigenvalues are unreliable here. The same evaluation yields a stability map over the horizon and the output-current weight that guides the tuning. In switching-level simulations of a 20 kW charger with 30% lower leakage inductance, the PI cascade and the non-adaptive MPC become unstable. The proposed controller keeps the grid-current total harmonic distortion at 2.3%. A compiled C implementation takes at most 5.1 µs per 10 µs control period on a desktop processor but 0.75–2.7 ms on a TMS320F28335 microcontroller, too slow for 100 kHz.

papers.title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite ( γ N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired γ N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting γ N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.

papers.title: Physics-grounded sequence-domain graph learning for adaptive fault location in IBR-dominated offshore wind farm transmission networks
papers.abstract: Abstract Fault location in offshore wind-farm networks dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) is complicated by converter-limited fault currents, cable charging currents and high fault resistance, which violate the assumptions of classical impedance-based estimators. This paper proposes PG-SDGL, a physics-grounded sequence-domain graph-learning framework that combines a graph-attention sequence-domain graph neural network (SeqGNN), a three-sequence physics-informed neural network (3Seq-PINN) for fault-resistance decoupling, sequence-residual split-conformal prediction intervals, cable charging-current compensation, an analytical IBR fault-current decomposition, a harmonic high-impedance-fault (HIF) gate with Dempster–Shafer fusion of two intelligent electronic devices and a protection-consistency index (PCI). The framework was evaluated in simulation on a 69 kV network with a 60 km overhead interconnection line and three 5–9 km submarine cable feeders, for four fault types and fault resistances of 2–150 Ω. Feeder-identification accuracy was 99.4–99.6%. Over 2–40 Ω, the average main-line mean relative error (MRE) was 0.195%, compared with 0.631% in the published random-forest benchmark on the same line model. The average fault-resistance mean absolute error decreased from 4.67 Ω (random-forest benchmark) to 2.07 Ω (single-sequence PINN) and 1.98 Ω (3Seq-PINN). The sequence-residual intervals reached 95.0–96.9% empirical coverage with a 33.8% smaller average normalized width than plain split-conformal intervals. At 150 Ω, HIF detection accuracy was 97.4%, location MRE was 1.48% and PCI was 0.924.

papers.title: Hybrid Intelligent Control for System Dynamic Regulation of Large Interconnected Power Systems Incorporating Electric Vehicles With Real‐Time Implementation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This article discusses the dynamic response regulation of contemporary power systems, focusing on hybrid configurations that integrate conventional and nonconventional energy sources. The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) and nonconventional energy sources, along with relevant system nonlinearities, complicates an existing power system. A strong controller is necessary for such a system to function correctly. A novel multistage control method based on model predictive control is provided for effective frequency management. The simulation findings indicate a notable reduction in system dynamics when comparing the proposed controller with traditional industrial controllers. A novel Pied Kingfisher Optimizer is applied as an optimization approach in dynamic control analysis. We also demonstrate how various energy storage techniques impact the system's dynamic control. This study provides a unique analysis illustrating the effects of the significant integration of EVs into the power grid. The proposed controller demonstrates excellent dependability across a variety of system configurations, even as energy consumption varies and renewable energy sources are unpredictable. Lastly, a real‐time simulator was used to model the developed power system with different secondary controllers.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The US DoD Inspector General's Audit of the F/A‐18 fleet and the US Government Accountability Office's report into the sustainment of the F35 fleet have focused attention on the effect of the environment on structural integrity. Since Boeing Space, Intelligence, and Weapons Systems (BSI&WS) laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Scalmalloy and LPBF 7A77, which are both additively manufactured aluminum alloys, are being considered for building limited‐life parts for military aircraft, this paper compares the effect of prior exposure to an aggressive environment on their durability and their equivalent initial damage sizes. We show that, whereas the 7A77 specimens had extensive corrosion after only 14 days of exposure to a 5% salt spray fog environment at 35°C, Scalmalloy showed little evidence of corrosion after 28 days. Subsequent fatigue tests found that 7A77 had a significantly lower fatigue life than Scalmalloy and that its fracture toughness was significantly lower than that of Scalmalloy.

papers.title: Domain-Knowledge-Guided Candidate Generation for Surrogate-Based Injection Molding Optimization
papers.abstract: Injection molding (IM) quality optimization involves coupled process variables, nonlinear quality responses, and a limited budget for physical trials. Numerical optimizers can use measured process data effectively, but they do not directly represent troubleshooting rules and other experience-based knowledge that is recorded in text. This study proposes large language model-based extended data-driven optimization (LLM-EDO), a domain-knowledge-guided framework for surrogate-based candidate generation. The framework converts process variables, quality curve discrepancies, feasible bounds, and retrieved expert cases into a structured request. A language model then proposes a bounded parameter vector, and a fixed long short-term memory surrogate evaluates the resulting quality curve. The framework is examined in a surrogate-in-the-loop environment using repeated and multi-start tests and is compared with Bayesian optimization, simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation, and knowledge-informed gradient-based SPSA. The reported runs show reductions in curve distance for the tested initial configurations and competitive terminal objective values. They also show run-to-run variability, and iteration counts are reported as decision rounds rather than wall-clock measurements. The results support the feasibility of domain-knowledge-guided candidate generation for surrogate-based quality curve matching under the tested process configurations.

papers.title: Estimation‐Driven Model Predictive Control Architecture for Active Suspension Systems Under Road Disturbances
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This research work presents an optimal control architecture for a quarter‐car active suspension system, which integrates a discrete‐time Kalman filter (KF) with a model predictive control (MPC) scheme. The proposed framework aims to enhance ride comfort and vehicle stability by effectively suppressing the impacts of road disturbances, that is, road bumps and pathholes, through a feasible control input. The proposed framework is based on an estimation‐based control architecture, where a KF provides an optimal reconstruction of the unmeasurable states. The estimated states information is then fed as input to the MPC scheme, which minimizes a cost function by solving a finite‐horizon constrained quadratic optimization problem to compute an optimal control input. The stability of the proposed control architecture is thoroughly investigated via a Lyapunov‐based analysis, with the MPC cost function serving as a Lyapunov candidate function. Computer simulations are carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, where the results for both real and estimated states confirm the minimum‐variance property of the KF. Furthermore, the results corresponding to the open‐loop and closed‐loop configurations demonstrate the efficiency of the closed‐loop optimal control strategy in state regulation, disturbance rejection, and control effort. In perturb scenarios, the performance parameters, such as oscillation suppression, settling time, and overshoot, are comparatively analyzed. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed control framework in damping undesired oscillations, with minimum overshoot and reduced settling times, thus improving ride comfort and vehicle stability.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control for a Multiport 4L NPC DAB Converter Under Unbalanced and No-Load Conditions
papers.abstract: Multilevel (ML) neutral-point-clamped (NPC) dual-active-bridge (DAB) topologies have emerged as a promising solution for multiport dc-dc power conversion systems. In particular, the 4L NPC DAB is a promising solution for the auxiliary power module (APM) in electric vehicles (EVs) featuring a multiple-voltage architecture in their auxiliary system (AS). By connecting three low-voltage (LV) battery modules between the 4L dc-link nodes, multiple dc ports with different operating voltages are obtained. Then, EV auxiliary loads can be grouped according to their optimum voltage ratings and supplied from three distinct-voltage dc ports. In this configuration, the main challenge is to regulate the state of charge (SoC) of the LV-battery modules. For this purpose, this paper proposes a moving-discretized-control-set model predictive control (MDCS-MPC) for a 2L–4L NPC DAB in the EV APM application. The proposed control strategy combines the adjustment of modulation angles with the use of redundant switching patterns to regulate the LV-battery modules SoC in a wide operating range, including no-load conditions in the partial-voltage dc ports. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments verify the real-time performance of the proposed control.

papers.title: Direct observation of surface chemistry evolution for Ti-6Al-4V powders in calciothermic reduction recycling process
papers.abstract: Abstract Titanium alloy powders are susceptible to oxygen pickup during handling, storage, and usage in additive manufacturing (AM), which degrades the 3D-printed parts’ mechanical properties and severely limits their reuse. Industrial AM titanium alloy feedstocks are subjected to stringent oxygen requirements, leading to large volumes of high-oxygen powder waste, which increases carbon footprint and cost. Thermochemical reduction with strong oxygen-affinity metals offers a viable route for titanium powder recovery, yet the oxygen removal mechanism from powder surfaces remains to be confirmed by direct experimental observation. Here, calciothermic reduction of AM-grade spherical Ti-6Al-4V powder is performed, followed by acid pickling and drying. Multiscale characterization is employed to correlate changes in bulk oxygen content, surface morphology, oxide-layer structure, and near-surface chemistry at the individual-particle level. Atom probe tomography reveals a graded oxygen profile extending from a TiO₂ outer surface through progressively oxygen-depleted subsurface regions into the α-Ti64 matrix. The oxidized and rejuvenated powders exhibit oxide regions of approximately 10 and <5 nm, respectively, while the matrix oxygen concentration decreased from about 3.2 to 0.5 at.%. A Ca–O-rich reaction-product layer and a narrow Ca–Ti–O interfacial region were directly observed after reduction, indicating that oxygen transfer occurs through a surface-mediated interfacial reaction.

papers.title: RiskGuard: a card-based serious game for enhancing education on security patterns and software vulnerabilities in web systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Software security education is still insufficiently addressed in many undergraduate computing curricula. Programs often emphasize attack-oriented activities rather than secure design practices, leaving future developers with limited skills to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities. Active learning approaches, such as serious games, offer opportunities to foster engagement and practical understanding of secure development concepts. We aim to design and evaluate RiskGuard , a card-based serious game that supports the teaching of software vulnerabilities and security patterns, investigating its impact on students’ knowledge, intrinsic motivation, and learning experience. We conducted a controlled experiment with 32 undergraduate students from Systems Analysis and Development (SAD) and Information Security (IS) programs. Participants were assigned to either a traditional lecture or a lecture followed by a RiskGuard session. Learning and motivation were assessed using a Knowledge Assessment Questionnaire and the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI), complemented by qualitative feedback. Our results indicate that RiskGuard supported concept reinforcement and increased students’ engagement and intrinsic motivation, although it did not outperform lecture-only instruction in immediate knowledge-assessment scores. RiskGuard shows potential as a complementary educational tool for promoting secure software design through game-based learning. This study contributes (i) the design and open resources of RiskGuard , (ii) empirical evidence on its learning and motivational effects, and (iii) insights for integrating serious games into cybersecurity and software engineering education.

papers.title: Co-adaptive learning and domain adaptation bridge the translational gap in neuroprosthetic control: a review
papers.abstract: Myoelectric and neural prosthetic devices frequently fail in daily clinical use despite laboratory success, a persistent translational gap driven by domain shift, the non-stationary nature of biological signals arising from neural plasticity, motor learning, muscle fatigue, and electrode displacement. This comprehensive review synthesizes the neurophysiological and technical origins of domain shift and evaluates algorithmic strategies developed to accommodate it. We identify that domain shift stems from coupled biological and technical processes, including cross-session drift and anatomical variability. Algorithmic countermeasures, such as closed-loop decoder adaptation, adaptive filtering, ensemble modeling, reinforcement learning, and transfer learning, address distinct facets of this problem, balancing adaptation speed against system stability. Crucially, we emphasize co-adaptive systems where decoder updates interact directly with ongoing neural and motor plasticity. Evidence indicates that treating the user as a passive signal source limits long-term control; instead, the user must be viewed as an active learning partner. Sustained improvements in neuroprosthetic reliability require integrating multiple adaptation strategies within a translational neuro-engineering framework that respects biological timescales. This integrated approach may help reduce long-term prosthetic device abandonment and advance accessible, robust assistive neurotechnology for clinical populations worldwide.
