papers.title: Discrepancies and Consistencies in Multi-Source Estimates of Eurasian Spring Snowmelt During 1982–2014
papers.abstract: Snow alters land–atmosphere energy and moisture exchanges via albedo and hydrological effects, markedly impacting subseasonal-to-seasonal climate variability. While Earth observations and model-based products form the foundation for investigating snow–climate interactions, comprehensive assessments of snowmelt, which directly reflects snow-induced hydrological and thermal anomalies, remain scarce compared to those of conventional snow mass variables. Benchmarked against the satellite–in situ blended GlobSnow data, this study comprehensively evaluates the discrepancies and consistencies of Eurasian spring snowmelt (spring snow water equivalent difference, SSD) across six multi-source datasets (SnowCCI, JRA-3Q, ERA5-Land, MERRA-2, GLDAS-NOAH, and FLDAS) during 1982–2014. The results reveal that satellite-based SnowCCI and JRA-3Q exhibit the highest consistency with GlobSnow in reproducing the spatial distribution, temporal variability, and dominant east–west dipole mode of Eurasian SSD. Specifically, they accurately capture its clear latitudinal zonation and a distinct dipole-like trend, characterized by decreasing SSD over western Eurasia and increasing SSD over eastern Eurasia. Conversely, ERA5-Land and MERRA-2 reasonably capture the temporal evolution of SSD but tend to overestimate variability amplitudes. GLDAS-NOAH exhibits relatively weak regional heterogeneity and underestimates SSD variability, whereas FLDAS tends to overestimate variability amplitudes and shows pronounced regional dependence. Further analysis suggests that uncertainties in snowfall simulations may be a major source of discrepancies in SSD estimation, although their relative contribution remains uncertain. These findings provide crucial insights for selecting appropriate datasets in snow–climate research and underscore the importance of dataset uncertainty quantification in subseasonal-to-seasonal climate prediction.

papers.title: Configuration over Architecture: Deep Learning Models for Daily Streamflow Forecasting in Snowmelt-Dominated Watersheds of Southwestern Alberta
papers.abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasting in snowmelt-dominated headwaters is critical for flood mitigation, reservoir operations, and water resource management, yet it remains challenging due to non-linear interactions among snowmelt dynamics, meteorological forcing, and watershed hydrology. This study evaluates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for daily streamflow prediction in three mountainous watersheds of southwestern Alberta and systematically examines the sensitivity of model performance to key configuration decisions, including timestep selection, feature engineering, seasonal period, adjacent gauge inclusion, weather forecasting, and attention mechanisms. Results demonstrate high predictive accuracy of up to 0.98 NSE for typical daily streamflow when the models are optimally configured. However, all models substantially underpredicted a 1995 extreme flood event by 44–78%, reflecting the inherent challenge of predicting rare events with imbalanced training data. The extreme-event underprediction was masked by aggregate evaluation metrics over a typical flow period, which necessitated a separate evaluation for the extreme event in the LSTM performance evaluation. These findings provide guidance for configuring LSTM models for small watersheds and highlight data augmentation and uncertainty quantification as future directions for improving extreme event predictions.

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Sequential Experimental Design of Metallurgical Solid-Waste-Based Gel Materials for Cemented Paste Backfill
papers.abstract: Cemented paste backfill (CPB) provides a pathway for utilizing metallurgical solid wastes, in which blended precursor constituents hydrate and develop strength-bearing gel products within the hardened backfill. Screening multi-component formulations is experimentally intensive because each candidate requires preparation, curing, and multi-age strength testing. The primary contribution of this study is a data-driven virtual experimental environment that integrates multi-age UCS surrogates, constrained chemistry-to-recipe mapping, cost and feasibility evaluation, and Markovian campaign updates. This environment is used to investigate sequential experimental-design strategies for balancing strength, cost, and recipe feasibility. Forty-eight measured mixtures comprising five gel-forming precursor constituents, four process variables, and 3-, 7-, and 28-day uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) were used to construct age-specific surrogate models. A chemistry-space representation based on six major oxides was introduced, and candidate chemistries were mapped to executable formulations through constrained optimization. Sequential formulation design was cast as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and investigated using reinforcement learning (RL) and query-by-committee active learning (AL). Each campaign comprised 50 surrogate-generated virtual queries; no additional specimens were prepared for these campaign evaluations. Under normal supply, LSTM-based RL obtained the highest five-seed mean dimensionless strength-cost score (0.1895), equivalent to 84.8% of the optimistic PSO reference; the best AL configuration reached 0.1753. A supplementary 50-seed virtual comparison yielded 0.1818 versus 0.1729 (paired t-test, p = 0.0064). AL and RL were statistically unresolved when steel slag was unavailable, whereas AL retained a higher fraction of the case-specific PSO reference after the EAF reduction-slag price doubled. Randomized feed-chemistry simulations further showed that the workflow can re-project target chemistries and identify feasible candidates within the domain represented by the surrogate data. The resulting computational environment supports efficient screening of sequential design strategies and prioritization of promising precursor recipes for subsequent laboratory preparation, strength verification, and hydrate-gel characterization.

papers.title: Engineering Education Research and Skills for Future Development: A Comparative Modelling Study of Curriculum Configurations Under Varying Institutional Capacity
papers.abstract: Engineering graduates are entering a workplace where knowing the technical fundamentals is no longer enough. Employers increasingly look for graduates who can solve unfamiliar problems, make sound design decisions, work confidently with digital tools, communicate clearly, and continue learning without constant supervision. This paper describes a controlled modelling study that compares four curriculum approaches: a lecture-centred baseline, active learning augmentation, project-based learning organised around CDIO principles, and industry-integrated project-based learning. All four are assessed using the same seven-domain competency framework, developed from accreditation criteria and published evidence on employer skill needs. To keep the comparison fair, the same simulated learner cohort is passed through every approach rather than generating a different cohort for each one. Three hundred cohorts are simulated under each of three institutional capacity conditions: well-resourced, moderately-resourced, and constrained. The study reports a composite competency attainment index, the percentage of the employer-referenced gap that is closed, a simulated delivery-cost index, ninety-five percent confidence intervals, and matched non-parametric statistical tests. Under well-resourced settings, the model gives mean attainment values of 60.11 for the baseline, 62.81 for active learning augmentation, 64.85 for project-based learning, and 65.97 for industry-integrated project-based learning, with Kendall's W = 0.429 and p < 0.001 in the Friedman test. As institutional resources become constrained, however, this ordering becomes less distinct. In the constrained scenario, the advantage of industry-integrated delivery falls to 2.70 index points, and the difference from project-based learning is no longer statistically separable after Holm adjustment at the 0.05 level. Active learning augmentation also retains much of its benefit while requiring considerably less simulated cost. The sensitivity analysis places the crossover between industry-integrated and project-based learning at about eighty-five students per staff member. Beyond that point, the most resource-intensive approach no longer produces the highest simulated attainment. These numbers come from a model input-based simulation, not from observations of an actual programme or student cohort. The aim is therefore to make the underlying reasoning transparent and repeatable, and to show when the additional effort required by high-contact teaching is supported by the model.

papers.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in industrial environments require autonomous surveying capabilities that jointly support scene understanding, safe locomotion, and manipulation-oriented perception. However, existing active reconstruction and model predictive control methods are typically separated, making it difficult to propagate perception uncertainty into motion decisions or prioritize observations according to downstream manipulation value. This paper proposes UNF-WMPC, an uncertainty-aware neural-field whole-body model predictive control framework integrating semantic neural-field reconstruction, task-weighted information gain, receding-horizon viewpoint optimization, and whole-body safety constraints. The method models reconstruction uncertainty, predicts its reduction under candidate future observations, and incorporates uncertainty-dependent clearance, balance, joint, collision, and human-separation constraints into the control loop. Experiments on four indoor datasets show that UNF-WMPC consistently improves reconstruction quality, information-acquisition efficiency, surveying safety, and robustness under progressive perception degradation compared with active reconstruction baselines. These results demonstrate that coupling task-oriented perception with predictive whole-body control provides an effective foundation for reliable humanoid surveying and subsequent industrial manipulation.

papers.abstract: In the context of high uncertainty and turbulence of the Russian stock market, scientifically based approaches to assessing the investment attractiveness of public companies are of particular importance, taking into account both fundamental operational indicators and a wide range of external macroeconomic, competitive, regulatory and geopolitical factors. This study is devoted to the development of an innovative methodology that integrates traditional methods of multiplicative and discounted analysis with modern machine learning algorithms and stochastic modeling, which allows us to move from point estimates to probabilistic intervals of fair value, adaptive to changing market regimes. The paper systematizes 50 key cost drivers, divided into endogenous (operational and financial metrics, logistics infrastructure, monetization) and exogenous (macroeconomic indicators, competitive environment, regulatory changes, force majeure), and using methods of gradient boosting, LASSO regression and Bayesian optimization, their weight ranges are determined, which allowed to build a multi-level hierarchy of influence on the market capitalization. The proposed system of eight interrelated mathematical formulas includes stochastic dynamics of key indicators (turnover, operating profit, customer base), nonlinear interactions between growth drivers, multiplicative adjustments to geopolitical and competitive risks (taking into account the GPR and EPU indices), corporate governance awards, ESG rating, technological sovereignty and intellectual property, and There is also discounting of projected free cash flows over the medium-term horizon. Dynamic calibration of the weights is carried out through a multifactorial regime classifier that takes into account market volatility, inflation differential, business activity and technical indicators, which ensures that the model adapts to different phases of the economic cycle. Practical verification based on historical data (2010-2026) showed high predictive accuracy (R2=0.93, RMSE≈135 rubles, MAPE=3.8%), and the final confidence interval of the fair value of shares obtained using the Bayesian approach demonstrated the practical applicability of the developed tool for substantiating investment decisions, risk management and scenario planning in conditions of high uncertainty.

papers.title: A Strain-Driven PINN Incorporating Constitutive Models for Unsaturated Soils
papers.abstract: The hydraulic and mechanical properties of unsaturated soils are relatively complex. To address the highly nonlinear hydro-mechanical behavior of unsaturated soils, this study proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model constrained by the constitutive model of unsaturated soils. Driven by axial strain, the model uses a fully connected neural network to predict five variables, including axial stress, suction, effective saturation, void ratio and confining pressure. The constitutive relationships of soil-water characteristic curves, and boundary conditions are all embedded in the loss function to ensure that the predictions comply with physical laws. The model was validated by using unsaturated triaxial test data under various overconsolidation ratios and suction conditions. Sensitivity analysis indicated that λ = 0.1 yielded the lowest combined error among the candidate weights examined, indicating a high agreement between the predicted results and experimental data. The established model can reproduce the deviator stress and volumetric changes in unsaturated expansive soil under different stress histories, and the model demonstrates promising prediction performance across the investigated strain stages under the available triaxial test conditions. Comparisons with the MLP baseline and a conventional constitutive model indicate that the proposed PINN can reproduce the main trends in the investigated hydro-mechanical responses.

papers.title: Contribuições da reabilitação fisioterapêutica na capacidade funcional e força muscular após artroplastia total de quadril: revisão integrativa.
papers.abstract: Introduction: After total hip arthroplasty, patients may experience reduced muscle strength, gait impairments, and difficulties performing daily activities. Objective: To identify the physiotherapy rehabilitation protocols used to restore functional capacity and muscle strength in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty. Materials and Methods: An integrative literature review was conducted, comprising ten studies on physiotherapy rehabilitation after the procedure. The interventions and their outcomes related to muscle strength and functional capacity were analyzed. Results: The identified protocols included progressive resistance training, joint mobilization and early ambulation, gait and balance training, elliptical trainer exercise, and home-based programs with remote follow-up. Resistance training performed before and after surgery showed favorable outcomes for strength, gait, and function. Elliptical trainer exercise contributed to knee extensor strength and walking performance. In-person and home-based programs improved function, with no consistent superiority of one approach over the other. Conclusion: The physiotherapy protocols analyzed contributed to functional and muscular recovery after total hip arthroplasty. Differences among interventions and outcomes prevented the identification of a single superior protocol, indicating that exercises should be tailored to each patient’s impairments and progress.

papers.title: Psychological processes of posttraumatic growth among caregivers of children with autism: a qualitative-dominant study informed by the stress-reactive rumination model
papers.abstract: Introduction Caregivers of children with autism face prolonged care responsibilities and uncertainty about future support. Although rumination has been associated with posttraumatic growth (PTG), less is known about how caregivers describe recurring thoughts and perceived growth in the context of long-term caregiving. Guided by the stress-reactive rumination model, this qualitative-dominant study explored caregivers' accounts of perceived PTG and the psychological processes they described during long-term caregiving. Methods Fifteen primary caregivers, recruited from two rehabilitation-related institutions in southeastern China, participated in semi-structured interviews. Interviews were analyzed using an iterative, theory-informed, codebook-oriented thematic analysis. Two researchers independently coded the transcripts, developed and refined a codebook, and resolved coding discrepancies through discussion with a third researcher. PTGI dimension scores were summarized descriptively to contextualize the qualitative findings, with the stress-reactive rumination model serving as a sensitizing framework during interpretation. Results Three interrelated themes were developed: (1) diagnostic shock and negative attribution, involving self-blame and catastrophic interpretations; (2) being trapped by the future, involving concerns about future independence, continuity of care, and perceived lack of support; and (3) moving from distress to active coping, involving active learning, self-regulation, acceptance, and meaning reconstruction. PTGI dimension means were highest for personal strength (4.38) and appreciation of life (4.22). The findings suggest that caregivers' accounts of growth were not a simple transition from distress to recovery. Rather, many caregivers reported ongoing future-oriented worries while concurrently describing practical coping strategies, enhanced personal strength, and renewed meaning in caregiving. The stress-reactive rumination model helped interpret these accounts by highlighting a possible shift in rumination direction—from self-blame and future-oriented fear toward actionable concerns and meaning reconstruction. Conclusion The study contributes to existing caregiver resilience research by integrating PTGI descriptive data with qualitative themes in a Chinese caregiving context. The study illustrates that caregiver growth is not a straightforward transition from distress to recovery, but an uneven experience shaped by both individual coping and the challenges of long-term caregiving.

papers.title: Pathology-Triggered Cascade-Responsive Implants for Converting Diabetic Microenvironment Signals Into Osteogenic Drivers.
papers.abstract: Hyperglycemia severely impairs implant osseointegration due to a hostile bone microenvironment of glycemic fluctuations and oxidative stress. Although responsive biomaterials can dynamically regulate pathological issues, converting harmful signals into a continuous driving force that promotes bone formation remains challenging. Herein, we present a cascade-responsive poly(aryl ether sulfone ketone) (PPESK) implant designed to actively leverage pathological signals for bone regeneration. PPESK features a chitosan-based surface modified with glucose oxidase (GOD), encapsulating black phosphorus (BP)-based nanoparticles loaded with in situ mineralized IGF-1 (mBI). Underlying this design is a glucose/pH/ROS cascade-responsive mechanism where local glucose triggers the catalytic activity of GOD, leading to acid-induced swelling of chitosan and subsequent exposure of mBI. Subsequently, the intrinsic oxidative responsiveness of BP to reactive oxygen species (ROS) facilitates the controlled release of IGF-1. It not only utilizes pathological signal transduction for targeted drug delivery to enhance the osteogenic differentiation potential of BMSCs but also establishes a self-regulated feedback path. By continuously consuming excess glucose and ROS, the implant improves the adverse local environment while promoting bone regeneration. Consequently, the PPESK implant accelerates bone remodeling in vivo, transforming the hyperglycemic microenvironment into an active driver for diabetic bone regeneration and offers a novel therapeutic strategy for stagnated bone repair.
